newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps - CFDs still slide, others steady.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps - CFDs still slide, others steady.

text.p: European oil swaps were mixed on Wednesday with Brent crude CFDs continuing to lose ground while product swaps were either steady or a touch stronger.

Brent CFDs slipped to +2.5 cents against July for the balance of this week from 4.00 cents over yesterday while further out weeks dropped even more sharply. June 2-6 was pegged -30 cents against July from -22.5 cents while June 9-13 was -26 cents from 22.5 cents.
Traders said Dated Brent was offered between flat and -10 cents to July with a June 12-14 cargo offered around July -10. A deal was concluded yesterday at July +3.

High sulphur fuel oil swaps staged a slight recovery despite very aggresive selling early that saw physical barges going for as low as $77 and $77.50 fob ARA in what many in the market saw as the result of pricing against a Russian cargo.
Swaps bounced back $1.00 or so from Wednesday to hover around June value $82 with July about $83.50.
Gasoline took a breather as the market waited for direction from the U.S. June was bid at $204 and offered at $205, steady against Wednesday.
Naphtha was a touch firmer with some speculation that crude's fall was overdone. June sapws were pegged around $189 and July at $189.50.
